The **2022–23 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team** represented the [University of Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tennessee "University of Tennessee") in the [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season")[college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") season. Led by former Lady Vol [Kellie Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellie_Harper "Kellie Harper"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-1) entering her fourth year as head coach, the team played its games at [Thompson–Boling Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thompson%E2%80%93Boling_Arena "Thompson–Boling Arena") as members of the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference").

The Lady Vols finished the season with a 25–12 overall record, 13–3 in the conference. They advanced to the finals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 SEC women's basketball tournament"), where they lost to South Carolina.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-2) Finishing strong in the conference, the Lady Vols earned an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), advancing to the Sweet Sixteen before losing to Virginia Tech.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

## Previous season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Previous season")]

The [2021–22 team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team "2021–22 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team") finished the season 25–9, 11–5 in third place in SEC play. They lost in the semifinals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 SEC women's basketball tournament") to their rivals, Kentucky,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-4) who went on to win the tournament. The Lady Vols also received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), where they lost in the Sweet Sixteen to Louisville.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-5)
